findings.title: Invalid ERB syntax breaks rendering of embed/best
findings.body: The tag `<%- end if %>` expands to invalid Ruby (`end if`) after the if/else block. Rendering `best` when a topic exists raises SyntaxError and returns 500, so the embedded comments view cannot be displayed.

findings.title: Imported URL is interpolated into raw HTML unsafely
findings.body: The imported URL is placed directly into an `<a href='#{url}'>` footer without HTML escaping. Because the post is created with `cook_method: raw_html`, this footer becomes rendered HTML and is emitted with `raw` in the embed view. A URL containing `'`, `">`, or event-handler markup can execute stored XSS when the post is viewed. Escape the URL before interpolation.

findings.title: RSS/Atom feed content is stored and rendered as unsanitized raw HTML
findings.body: `i.content` is unescaped with `CGI.unescapeHTML` and passed to `TopicEmbed.import`, which sets `cook_method: raw_html`; `Post#cook` then returns the raw content unchanged and the embed view renders it with `raw`. A malicious or compromised feed can include `<script>`, event-handler attributes, or `javascript:` URLs, resulting in stored XSS on the Discourse site. Sanitize the feed HTML or use the normal cooking pipeline.

findings.title: RSS `content` may be nil with no fallback
findings.body: Many RSS/Atom feeds provide the entry body in `description`, `summary`, or `content:encoded`, so SimpleRSS may leave `content` as nil. The code calls `i.content.scrub`, which raises `NoMethodError` and aborts the whole poll. Use a fallback such as `i.content || i.description || i.summary`.

findings.title: absolutize_urls drops explicit ports 80/443 incorrectly for the wrong scheme
findings.body: The condition `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` is independent of the URL scheme. For `http://example.com:443/...` the port is omitted, rewriting relative links to port 80; for `https://example.com:80/...` the port is omitted, rewriting them to port 443. Compare against the scheme's default port, for example using `uri.default_port`.

findings.title: import_remote uses HTTP open without requiring open-uri
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` on an HTTP URL, but this file does not require `open-uri`. If no other code loaded it, Kernel#open treats the URL as a filesystem path and raises `Errno::ENOENT`. Callers such as `TopicRetriever` and the Disqus import can reach this path. Add `require 'open-uri'`.

findings.title: Update path assumes the associated post still exists
findings.body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is used without a nil check. The `belongs_to :post` association has no guarantee that the post still exists, and posts can be deleted. If `embed.post` is nil, `PostRevisor.new(post)` and subsequent calls on nil will raise. The importer should recreate the post or explicitly handle the missing record.

findings.title: Concurrent imports for the same URL race and hit unique index
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` is checked before the create transaction. Two concurrent jobs can both see no existing embed, both create topics/posts, and then the second `TopicEmbed.create!` fails on the unique index on `embed_url`, causing job failure. Re-check inside the transaction or rescue `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and re-fetch the existing embed.

findings.title: request.referer is interpolated into JavaScript without escaping
findings.body: `request.referer` is inserted directly into a JavaScript string. The controller only validates the host part of the referer, so a page on the allowed host whose URL contains a quote can break out of the JS string and execute script in the Discourse iframe's origin. Escape it with `j(request.referer)` or `escape_javascript`.
